lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: wiping up and putting away

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 3 — kitchen helper safety and no-heat preparation
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice wiping up and putting away. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Thinking back to the last time they or someone else helped in the kitchen, the learner walks through a four-step wiping-and-putting-away routine on a real counter or table that has a cup, bowl, or spoon left on it: moving the dishes near the sink first, wiping the cleared surface with a damp cloth, returning small tools to their exact drawer or shelf, and doing one final look-over before calling the space done.
safetyNotes: Always ask a trusted adult before rinsing or touching any dish that might have been used with raw food.
Stick to non-sharp items like cups, bowls, and spoons; leave any knife for an adult to handle.
materials: learner-local: a drawer or shelf where small tools belong

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain specifically how today's four-step cleanup would have prevented the thing you noticed was left undone earlier.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Cleanup sequence: Completes all four steps (dishes near sink, wipe, tools returned, final look-over) in a working order. | Specificity of correction: Names a specific item or spot that was left out or undone. | Tool return accuracy: Returns each small tool to its correct drawer or shelf. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner apply the same four-step wiping-and-putting-away routine to a different shared space, like a bathroom counter after brushing teeth or a craft table after a project, naming what changes and what stays the same about the routine.

resources.title: wiping up and putting away coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Thinking back to the last time they or someone else helped in the kitchen, the learner walks through a four-step wiping-and-putting-away routine on a real counter or table that has a cup, bowl, or spoon left on it: moving the dishes near the sink first, wiping the cleared surface with a damp cloth, returning small tools to their exact drawer or shelf, and doing one final look-over before calling the space done.
Coach direction: Think back to the last time you or someone else helped in the kitchen.
Learner prompt: Name one specific thing that got left out or not put away after that task.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: wiping up and putting away complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Run the four-step wiping-and-putting-away routine in order: move dishes near the sink, wipe the cleared surface with a damp cloth, return small tools to their exact spot, and finish with a final look-over.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I rinsed and stacked any cup, bowl, or spoon near the sink instead of leaving it on the counter.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I wiped the counter or table surface with a damp cloth until crumbs and spills were gone.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I returned small tools, like a spoon or a measuring cup, to the exact drawer or shelf they belong in.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I did one final look-over of the whole space before calling it done.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: wiping up and putting away minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain specifically how today's four-step cleanup would have prevented the thing you noticed was left undone earlier.

Success checks: Cleanup sequence: Completes all four steps (dishes near sink, wipe, tools returned, final look-over) in a working order. | Specificity of correction: Names a specific item or spot that was left out or undone. | Tool return accuracy: Returns each small tool to its correct drawer or shelf.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: wiping up and putting away supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional wiping up and putting away condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Cleanup sequence: Completes all four steps (dishes near sink, wipe, tools returned, final look-over) in a working order. | Specificity of correction: Names a specific item or spot that was left out or undone. | Tool return accuracy: Returns each small tool to its correct drawer or shelf..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
